sections.overview: This geometrid moth occurs across much of Europe and adjoining parts of Asia and North Africa, with local records varying greatly by region.
sections.identification: The adult has several fine transverse wing lines, the pattern reflected in its scientific epithet and English name Many-lined moth.
sections.habitat: Its documented European habitats include open grassy and disturbed places where bedstraws of the genus Galium grow.
sections.diet: The caterpillar feeds on Galium species, including heath bedstraw, Galium saxatile.
sections.behavior: Adults fly from late afternoon into dusk and are also attracted to artificial lights.
sections.reproduction: The species has several adult generations in a year, and the pupa overwinters in a cocoon among plant debris.
sections.ecology: Its larval association with bedstraws ties its local occurrence to host-plant patches in suitable open vegetation.
sections.conservation: It is described as very rare and highly localized in Belgium, a regional observation that does not by itself establish global threat status.
